projects.name: Bukit Jelutong Cluster Homes
projects.excerpt: Twelve cluster units taken from pad footings to handover, with the drainage and roof falls detailed before a single wall went up.
projects.body:
A twelve-unit cluster scheme on soft ground near Bukit Jelutong. The site investigation came back poor enough that we revised the footing layout before pricing, which added three weeks at the start and saved an argument about settlement later. Roof falls, gutter sizing and the surface drainage were all set out at foundation stage rather than retrofitted.

All twelve units handed over inside the contract period with a short defect list, mostly paint and ironmongery.

projects.name: Sunway Mentari Retail Fit-Out
projects.excerpt: A ground-floor retail unit stripped back and fitted out to the tenant's brand standard, working nights to keep the centre trading.
projects.body:
The unit had been empty for a year and the previous tenant's M&E was unusable. We stripped it back to the shell, re-ran electrical and air-conditioning, and built the shopfront, ceiling and joinery to the tenant's brand pack.

Centre management only allowed noisy works between 10pm and 6am, so the programme was built around night shifts. The unit handed over two days early and opened on the planned date.

projects.name: Taman Melawati Shophouse Restoration
projects.excerpt: A row of four tired shophouses re-roofed, re-rendered and repainted, keeping the original facade details intact.
projects.body:
Four adjoining shophouses with failed roofs, spalling render and thirty years of ad-hoc signage. The brief was to make them watertight and presentable without flattening the original facade detail.

We re-roofed all four, cut out and replaced the spalled render, re-formed the gutters at a proper fall, and repainted to a palette the owner picked from the original scheme. The timber shutters were repaired rather than replaced where they were sound.

projects.name: Puchong Prima Double-Storey Extension
projects.excerpt: A rear double-storey extension on a standard terrace, with new beams, a re-laid slab and a re-worked wet kitchen.
projects.body:
A straightforward rear extension on a 20x70 terrace, made less straightforward by the original builder's rear beam, which was not sized for what the owner wanted to put on it.

We replaced the beam, poured a new slab, extended both floors, and reworked the wet kitchen and rear drainage at the same time. The family stayed in the house throughout, so the works were sequenced to keep one bathroom and the dry kitchen live.

faqs.a: Most jobs start within two to three weeks of you accepting the quote. We will tell you honestly at quoting stage if our crews are committed further out than that — we would rather lose the job than hold a slot we cannot keep.

faqs.q: Do you charge for a quote?
faqs.a: No. The site visit, measure-up and written quote are free anywhere in the Klang Valley. If the job needs a structural engineer's input before we can price it, we will say so and tell you what that costs before anything is commissioned.

faqs.q: What does a renovation actually cost in 2026?
faqs.a: As a rough guide: a bathroom strip-out and rebuild runs RM 18,000 to RM 35,000, a wet and dry kitchen reconfiguration RM 45,000 to RM 90,000, and a rear double-storey extension RM 160,000 upward depending on span and finishes. Your written quote will be specific; these are starting points, not a price list.

faqs.q: Do you handle the local authority submission?
faqs.a: For works that need it, yes — we prepare the drawings and support the submission to MBPJ, MBSA, DBKL or MPK. Approval timelines are the council's, not ours, so we build that waiting period into the programme rather than pretending it does not exist.

faqs.q: Will the monsoon delay my job?
faqs.a: External works slow down between October and March. We programme roofing, external render and drainage outside the worst of it where we can, and we tell you up front which parts of your job are weather-dependent.

Twelve months on workmanship from the handover date, plus whatever the manufacturer gives on materials — typically ten to fifteen years on membranes and roof sheets. Call us during the warranty period and we come back out.

about.missionBody: Malaysian construction has a reputation problem, and most of it is earned: verbal quotes, moving prices, crews that disappear for a fortnight. We run the opposite way — written scope, fixed price, named supervisor, weekly updates, and a warranty we honour without an argument.
